headline: High prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from Aider’s shared git workspace and broad egress; LlamaFactory adds no isolation or verification layer.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes repo files and shares state via a git repo, so attacker-controlled content in the workspace can influence its prompts. LlamaFactory has no filesystem or clipboard surfaces, so it is not a bridge itself, but the pair still has a shared-file pathway through Aider’s repo access. This is not provably blocked.
conditions: IF untrusted text is placed in the shared git repository, Aider may ingest it as context.
IF LlamaFactory is used to generate content that is copied into repo files, Aider can parse it as instructions.
mitigations: Restrict Aider to a clean branch or throwaway repo.
Add a manual review step before Aider reads any generated file.
Keep untrusted content outside the shared workspace.
Use file allowlists for Aider inputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for repo content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider has broad network egress and handles model-provider API keys, so repository contents can leave the local machine through its configured backend. LlamaFactory itself shows no egress or file access, but the pair still exposes source code and git history through Aider’s default workflow. The blast radius includes sensitive code and history, so this is more than low.
conditions: IF Aider is pointed at a repository containing secrets or proprietary code, those contents can be sent to a model provider.
IF LlamaFactory is used to prepare prompts or artifacts that Aider ingests, those artifacts can also be transmitted by Aider.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the repo before running Aider.
Use a local-only model backend for Aider.
Run Aider on a scrubbed clone of the repository.
Rotate any exposed API keys after the session.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP scanning before outbound requests.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider can write the filesystem and modify git state, while LlamaFactory cannot write, modify git, or access files. That means there is no meaningful write-write conflict between the pair. The only overlap is read-only on Aider’s side, so the conflict surface is small.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory is replaced with a writable agent, concurrent git conflicts could emerge.
IF Aider is run in multiple terminals against the same repo, git contention increases.
mitigations: Serialize Aider sessions per repository.
Use separate branches for each session.
Commit frequently to reduce merge scope.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files.
requires-engineering: add repo locking in the orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate edits and commits, and LlamaFactory can supply upstream text or artifacts that Aider may treat as input. There is no documented verification layer between them, so erroneous or hallucinated content can cascade into committed code changes. LlamaFactory is not action-taking, which keeps this below high.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory-produced text is copied into Aider without review, Aider may commit incorrect changes.
IF Aider is allowed to auto-commit generated diffs, downstream consumers may treat them as authoritative.
mitigations: Require human review before commit.
Compare generated claims against source files.
Disable auto-commit for high-risk changes.
Use tests before accepting Aider output.
requires-engineering: add structured verification between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and show no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch. Aider handles model-provider API keys and may send code to third-party providers, but LlamaFactory shows no data handling or outbound flow. With no documented compliance mismatch, only a limited gap is visible.
conditions: IF Aider is configured to send regulated data to a noncompliant model provider, compliance risk increases.
IF the repository contains regulated data and Aider uploads it, policy violations may occur.
mitigations: Use a compliant provider for Aider.
Exclude regulated data from the repo.
Review retention settings on the model backend.
Document data-flow boundaries for the pair.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for outbound prompts.
